cards.note: Chubu plate is super unique because of the rounded shape, you can spot it from far away.
Transformers in Chubu are often attached with large triangle and horizontal bars.
You may sometimes find an orange arrow located above the top most pole plate in Chugoku.
The transformers in Chugoku, which have a cross-shaped bar attached in the middle of the pole, mounted by a full triangle, will have a long horizontal or short vertical insulator(s) at the end.
Chugoku plates will have usually written Energia in latin and sometimes they will include logo.
This pole top is unique to Chugoku, there is similar version that are more thicc so make sure the pole top is thin like the one on the image.
This infrastructural arrow informs drivers of where the shoulder line is when under snow, and is located almost exclusively in Hokkaido(You can find similar rarely in northern prefectures of Japan)
Hokkaido plate can be recognized by having a lot of numbers in rows of 2.
Silver horizontal plates with logo on the top right. NTT plates will be also horizontal(in Tohoku NTT plates are vertical, and only Tohoku plate is horizontal).
These attachments with an approximately 120-degree angle can commonly be found on poles in Kansai.

One of the hardest plate to recognize. Have different designs but will have Japanese written in the middle/or the right and then characters below it in rows of 2 and will usually have 2 numbers at the bottom left/right.

This tuning fork pole top, with a thin wire and horizontal bar below, is common in the Kansai region. Make sure it looks exactly the same with that little thing on the wires in the middle(idk how to call it lol)
Tall reflector with washed colors is exclusive to Kansai region.

The transformers in Kansai have either a straight or zigzag bar mounted on the bottom of a square. The transformer(s) will be mounted on the sides of that same square. (Tohoku transformers are mounted in similar way but the bar will be connected to top of the square)
Often silver and handwritten characters. Horizontal characters above three vertical digits.
Those insulators are unique to Kanto region and are easy to spot. They have black "hat" on top of white insulator.
Black meteor like looking insulator, from far might be confused with Kanto tall-black hat insulator but Kyushu one appears little more bulkier even from far.
Distinc logo(sometimes might be missing). Three numbers horizontally near the top, with 4 vertical characters below them on the right(1 kana and 3 numbers).
Transformers mounted opposite side of the pole with a straight bar mounted on the side of the pole with 3 insulators on one side at the end.(Okinawa has T shaped bar)
Guy wires that look like paddle are unique to Kyushu and Okinawa.
Protruding bumps, sometimes darker reflector in the middle. Can also be found in Okinawa.
Plate with multiple numbers and lines in between them. Often will have more than 2 plates.
Transformers mounted opposite side of the pole with a T shaped bar mounted on the side of the pole.(Kyushu has straight bar). Sometimes only 1 transformer is present.
The transformers in Shikoku, which also have a cross-shaped bar attached in the middle of the pole, mounted by a half triangle, will have “hat shaped” short horizontal insulators at the end.
These orange and black bands wrapped around poles can often be found in Shikoku.
Distinct logo that you can remember since it has 4 dots representing 4 prefectures of Shikoku.
6 small reflectors with a little strip "connecting" them in the middle.
Silver horizontal plates with logo in top left. NTT plate will be vertical.(In Hokuriku all the plates will be horizontal)
Gray/White and Gray/Yellow reflectors.
Yellow guardrails are exclusive to Yamaguchi prefecture.
